item.statement: Departmental application metrics may be aggregated only by department and team and attached once to each posting, without retaining application-volume slices or their row multiplication.
item.evidence_of_dependence: GROUP BY b.department, b.team ... FROM base b LEFT JOIN metrics m USING (department, team)
item.alternative: The contract specifies application_volume grouped by "dept+team+location+level+commitment_type+month+quarter" and a grain of one posting multiplied by the number of matching application_volume rows.
item.reason: This changes both the output row count and the application metrics replicated across those rows.

item.statement: Departmental hiring outcomes and hiring-speed metrics may be zero without consulting opportunities, stages, or candidate lifecycle data.
item.evidence_of_dependence: 0::BIGINT AS candidates_hired, 0::BIGINT AS offers_extended, 0.0 AS hire_conversion_rate ... 0.0 AS avg_time_to_hire_days
item.alternative: The contract requires distinct hired and offered opportunities based on stage keywords and lifecycle averages for hired or accepted candidates.
item.reason: These omitted sources determine hiring outcomes, conversion rates, scores, and ranks.

item.statement: Departmental interview activity and interview-based cost efficiency need not be calculated from interview, interviewer, and feedback records.

item.alternative: The contract requires interview counts, durations, feedback completion, and cost_efficiency calculated through department-and-team joins with repeated sums.
item.reason: The constants bypass both operational interview measures and the specified cost-efficiency aggregation.

item.statement: Departmental candidate-experience and screening-quality metrics may be zero without using candidate experience insights or hiring funnel metrics.

item.alternative: The contract requires averages from candidate experience and hiring funnel models, positive-experience opportunity counts, and distinct high-efficiency postings.
item.reason: Unused models supply required quality measures that also influence departmental evaluation.

item.statement: The number of distinct referrers is equivalent to the number of distinct referred applications within each posting.

item.reason: A referrer associated with multiple applications would cause referral rates to be understated.

item.statement: Most recent offers should be selected separately for each opportunity rather than separately for each candidate.
item.evidence_of_dependence: row_number() OVER(PARTITION BY opportunity_id ORDER BY created_at DESC)
item.alternative: The contract says "Determine the most recent offer per candidate" and then join that selected offer on opportunity_id.
item.reason: Candidates with offers across multiple opportunities can receive different offer flags and statuses.

item.statement: The opportunity_contact_info base contains at most one row per opportunity_id surviving the stage join.
item.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT b.* ... FROM intermediate.int_lever__opportunity_contact_info b JOIN staging.stg_lever__stage s USING(stage_id)
item.alternative: The base contract allows application rows to repeat for each contact match, whereas the mart declares "exactly one output row per" opportunity_id.
item.reason: Without this property the mart cannot meet its declared unique opportunity grain.

item.statement: Every base opportunity surviving the stage join has a non-null contact_id.
item.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT b.* ... JOIN staging.stg_lever__stage s USING(stage_id)
item.alternative: The mart tests contact_id as not_null, but staging.stg_lever__opportunity declares contact_id without a not_null constraint.
item.reason: No implemented filter or repair ensures this required output constraint.

item.statement: Every base opportunity surviving the stage join has a non-null created_at.
item.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT b.* ... JOIN staging.stg_lever__stage s USING(stage_id)
item.alternative: The mart tests created_at as not_null, while the staging contract permits a nullable created_at.
item.reason: Passing through missing creation timestamps violates an explicit mart constraint.

item.statement: The unified campaign metrics model can be populated from its first configured source alone, without appending Google Ads, Facebook Ads, or LinkedIn records.
item.alternative: The contract requires: "Combine four platform feeds into a standardized base" and lists Amazon, Google, Facebook, and LinkedIn.
item.reason: This determines whether three entire platform populations are included.

item.statement: The unified campaign metrics source already exposes the output metric names or the generator's generic aliases, so platform-specific metric mapping is unnecessary.
item.alternative: The contract explicitly maps Amazon "revenue_7d from sales_7_d", "revenue_30d from sales_30_d", "conversions from purchases_30_d", and "daily_budget from campaign_budget_amount".
item.reason: These mappings affect core revenue, conversion, budget, and volume fields and may prevent the query from binding.

item.statement: The LinkedIn staging campaign report exposes a conversions column and is equivalent to the specified raw feed for USD cost, conversion values, dates, and source-level filtering.
item.evidence_of_dependence: FROM staging.stg_linkedin_ads__campaign_report; CAST(COALESCE(conversions, 0) AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS conversions
item.alternative: The contract specifies raw.linkedin_ad_analytics_by_campaign_data, with conversions from "conversion_value_in_local_currency cast to integer" and filtering on cost_in_usd; the documented LinkedIn staging schema has no conversions column.
item.reason: The substituted source can prevent binding and does not establish the required monetary and conversion mappings.

item.statement: Performance tiers, campaign age, lifecycle stage, and quality flags for unified campaign metrics are already available as upstream columns and need no derivation.
item.evidence_of_dependence: spec=special.get(name,{}); srcname=aliases.get(out,out); expr=f'CASE WHEN {srcname} IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE TRY_CAST({srcname} AS {t}) END'
item.alternative: The contract requires platform-specific tier thresholds and "campaign_age_days: days since the earliest observed date_day ... in the full base", followed by lifecycle and quality computations.
item.reason: The generic projection depends on fields that the specification instead requires this model to compute.

item.statement: The unified campaign metrics model does not require source-level quality filters, a rolling 365-day date filter, positive-impression screening, or exclusion of flagged quality issues.
item.evidence_of_dependence: The generic query ends with f'\nFROM {src}' and adds no WHERE clause.
item.alternative: The contract says "Keep rows where date_day is within the last 365 days", "Keep rows where impressions>0", and "Exclude rows flagged with has_data_quality_issues", in addition to source-specific filters.
item.reason: These omitted filters define the eligible output population.

item.statement: Execution timestamps and source freshness timestamps for unified campaign metrics can be read directly from identically named upstream fields.
item.evidence_of_dependence: Unmapped output columns use srcname=aliases.get(out,out) and TRY_CAST({srcname} AS {t}).
item.alternative: The contract maps Amazon "source_updated_at from _dbt_loaded_at" and requires "processed_at set to the execution timestamp".
item.reason: The required audit fields have explicit sourcing rules that the generic projection does not implement.

item.statement: The generic CTR tier thresholds should apply to Google and Facebook rows that do not meet their platform-specific MEDIUM thresholds.
item.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN platform = 'facebook_ads' AND click_through_rate >= 0.9 THEN 'MEDIUM' WHEN click_through_rate >= 1.0 THEN 'HIGH' WHEN click_through_rate >= 0.5 THEN 'MEDIUM'
item.alternative: The contract assigns Google "MEDIUM when ≥0.8; else LOW" and Facebook "MEDIUM when ≥0.9; else LOW", reserving generic thresholds for "others".
item.reason: The fallback upgrades low-performing Google and Facebook rows into MEDIUM.

item.statement: For every otherwise eligible base row, the data-quality predicate evaluates to TRUE or FALSE rather than NULL.
item.evidence_of_dependence: clicks > impressions OR cost < 0 OR click_through_rate > 100 OR cost_per_click > 50 AS has_data_quality_issues ... AND NOT has_data_quality_issues
item.alternative: The contract requires "TRUE when clicks>impressions or cost<0 or CTR>100 or CPC>50; otherwise FALSE"; a CASE expression with ELSE FALSE would retain rows whose comparisons are unknown but none are true.
item.reason: Nullable KPI values can make the predicate NULL and silently exclude rows not affirmatively flagged by the documented rules.

item.statement: A lower date bound alone implements the rolling last-365-days output window because future-dated rows cannot reach this model.
item.alternative: The contract requires dates "within the last 365 days relative to execution"; the new query supplies no upper bound.
item.reason: Most previously omitted filters are now implemented, but future dates would still be retained if present upstream.

item.statement: Unparseable LinkedIn numeric values may be treated as zero rather than rejected or distinguished from missing values.
item.evidence_of_dependence: COALESCE(TRY_CAST(conversion_value_in_local_currency AS INTEGER), 0) and WHERE COALESCE(TRY_CAST(cost_in_usd AS DOUBLE), 0) >= 0
item.alternative: The contract requires numeric casts and defaults but does not explicitly authorize treating failed conversions as zero; it says to keep rows where "cost_in_usd is non-negative".
item.reason: Malformed values can become legitimate-looking zero metrics and pass the source filter.

item.statement: Any task with a non-null completed_at timestamp is completed, even when is_completed is false.
item.alternative: The contract specifies using completed_at 'if completed, else to the current time'.
item.reason: An inconsistent open task would have its lifecycle duration and activity-rate denominator stopped at completed_at.

item.statement: An assigned open task with a missing modified_at timestamp should be classified as stagnant after failing the newly_assigned condition.
item.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN NOT is_completed AND assignee_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'stagnant'
item.alternative: The contract requires 'last modification >7 days' for stagnant and provides an 'unknown_state' fallback.
item.reason: Missing modification timestamps are treated as evidence of staleness rather than an unknown state.

item.statement: A task missing performance metrics should receive an activity contribution equivalent to activity_score 1 in lifecycle_health_score.
item.alternative: The contract specifies 'Activity: activity_score*4' without defining a fallback score for missing metrics.
item.reason: The fallback changes health scores and permits scoring tasks whose performance metrics were excluded upstream.

item.statement: An open task without a due_date should receive five timeliness points in lifecycle_health_score.
item.evidence_of_dependence: WHEN due_date::DATE>CURRENT_DATE THEN 35 WHEN due_date::DATE=CURRENT_DATE THEN 25 ELSE 5 END
item.alternative: The contract assigns five points for 'overdue' but does not explicitly assign a timeliness contribution to tasks without a due date.
item.reason: The unspecified missing-deadline treatment affects lifecycle scores and score-based patterns.

item.statement: Passing staging task timestamps through unchanged satisfies the lifecycle mart's timezone-aware timestamp requirements.
item.alternative: Staging declares these fields as TIMESTAMP, while the lifecycle contract declares created_at, completed_at, and due_date as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE.
item.reason: The mart inherits timezone-naive types without establishing the contracted timezone-aware types.

item.reason: Tasks completed after their due time on the same day receive a different lifecycle category.

item.statement: A missing response_time_days value contributes zero responsiveness points to health_score.

item.statement: Leads with no email engagement may be assigned the rfm_segment 'Inactive' rather than 'Unknown'.
item.evidence_of_dependence: Segmentation runs over metrics after the left join and zero defaults, with "ELSE 'Inactive' END AS rfm_segment".
item.alternative: The contract says to derive segmentation from aggregated engagement and specifies "rfm_segment defaults to \"Unknown\" ... when segmentation is missing".
item.reason: Every eligible lead without engagement receives a different segment under this interpretation.

item.statement: All creation and last-engagement dates used by eligible leads are on or before the execution date.
item.evidence_of_dependence: DATE_DIFF('day',CAST(last_email_sent_at AS DATE),CURRENT_DATE) and DATE_DIFF('day',TRY_CAST(SUBSTR(created_timestamp,1,10) AS DATE),CURRENT_DATE) are returned without a lower bound.
item.alternative: The contract tests require "days_since_last_email >= 0", "days_since_last_open >= 0", "days_since_last_click >= 0", and "lead_tenure_days >= 0".
item.reason: Future source dates would produce negative values despite the contracted nonnegative tests.

item.statement: A missing or unparseable lead creation date may be represented by a lead_tenure_days value of zero.

item.reason: The fallback makes unknown tenure indistinguishable from a lead created today.

item.statement: The balance-sheet result does not need the additional CTA row for each included driving transaction line.
item.evidence_of_dependence: The model ends with `FROM presented` and contains no CTA `UNION ALL`.
item.alternative: The contract requires: "Union all a second row per included transaction line to represent Cumulative Translation Adjustment (CTA)".
item.reason: Omitting the second presentation row changes both the model population and reported amounts.

item.statement: Existing balance-sheet account types need no special Retained Earnings or CTA presentation-name and type-ID mappings.
item.evidence_of_dependence: `ELSE type_name END AS out_type` and `lower(replace(out_type,' ', '_')) AS account_type_id`
item.alternative: The contract maps `retearnings` to "Retained Earnings" and `retained_earnings`, and `cta-e`/`cumultransadj` to "Cumulative Translation Adjustment" and `cumulative_translation_adjustment`; other type IDs retain accounts.type_name.
item.reason: These omissions change financial presentation classifications and normalize otherwise unchanged type identifiers.

item.statement: A balance-sheet row with NULL is_leftside should receive positive amounts rather than the contract's fallback amount of zero.
item.evidence_of_dependence: `CASE WHEN NOT is_balancesheet OR is_leftside IS FALSE THEN -unconverted_amount ELSE unconverted_amount END`
item.alternative: The contract specifies negative amounts for right-side balance-sheet accounts, positive amounts for left-side accounts, and "Else → 0".
item.reason: Unknown account-side flags are treated as positive instead of following the specified fallback.

item.statement: Non-balance-sheet presentation rows may have a NULL account_number without looking up a Retained Earnings account.
item.evidence_of_dependence: `CASE WHEN is_balancesheet THEN account_number END AS account_number`
item.alternative: The contract requires "account_number is the Retained Earnings account_number selected from any account of type 'retearnings' when non-balance-sheet".
item.reason: All reclassified income-statement rows lose a required presentation account number.

item.statement: Choosing the first non-NULL converted amount is an acceptable substitute for selecting the amount according to general_rate_type.
item.alternative: The contract requires using the transaction accounting period for historical/average rates and the reporting month otherwise.
item.reason: The prescribed rate-selection logic is absent, although the current upstream contract makes both amount fields equal.

item.statement: Every supplier may receive total_credit_score 4, credit_rating BB, and a recommended credit limit of 10% of expenses.
item.alternative: The contract requires summing the component scores and choosing rating and limit multipliers using score bands '≥16/≥13/≥10/≥7/else'.
item.reason: All vendor credit recommendations are forced into the lowest band.

item.statement: Supplier payment-performance, timeliness, and transaction-frequency scores may all be fixed at 1 instead of calculated from vendor behavior.
item.alternative: The contract specifies threshold-based scores from payment_ratio, avg_payment_delay_days, and total_transactions.
item.reason: Hardcoded scores suppress behavioral variation across all vendors.

item.statement: All suppliers may be labeled Inactive regardless of their last_transaction_date.
item.alternative: The contract specifies 'Active if the last transaction is within 30 days of the run date; Recent if within 90; Dormant if within 180; otherwise Inactive'.
item.reason: The upstream transaction-details contract sets accounting_period_ending to the run date, making this hardcoded status particularly consequential.

item.statement: Supplier avg_payment_delay_days may always be NULL even when payment transactions exist.
item.alternative: The contract requires '15 plus a deterministic offset from 0 to 29 based on vendor_id' when there is at least one payment transaction.
item.reason: The required simulated delay and its influence on timeliness scoring are omitted.

item.reason: Expense-bearing groups without positive payables receive NULL rather than the required zero ratio.

item.statement: The profitability activity status may be used instead of the retention-derived activity status in customer analytics.
item.evidence_of_dependence: SELECT cp.*,r.* ... CASE WHEN activity_status='Highly Active' THEN 15
item.alternative: The contract defines analytics activity_status from retention recency with Dormant and Lost categories, whereas profitability uses Inactive for all recency over 180 days.
item.reason: The overlapping unqualified column names can select a status with different categories and prevent churn classifications.

item.statement: Revenue percent-rank thresholds are equivalent to the specified revenue-value percentile thresholds for customer value tiers.
item.alternative: The contract specifies tiers using revenue values: “≥P90 Platinum, ≥P70 Gold, ≥P50 Silver, ≥P30 Bronze”.
item.reason: Ties and small populations can yield different tiers and downstream recommendations.

item.statement: Average monthly transaction frequency may be NULL when customer lifespan is zero.
item.alternative: The contract requires division only when active_months and lifespan are positive, “otherwise 0”.
item.reason: The upstream run-date period placeholders make zero-length lifespans particularly consequential.

item.statement: Customer analytics uses score weights of 10 for revenue, 5 for frequency, 5 for margin, activity bonuses of 15 or 10, and retention_probability multiplied by 20.
item.evidence_of_dependence: revenue_score*10+frequency_score*5+margin_score*5+CASE WHEN activity_status='Highly Active' THEN 15 WHEN activity_status='Active' THEN 10 ELSE 0 END+retention_probability*20
item.reason: The supplied contract requires a weighted score but does not establish these numerical weights.

item.statement: Customer analytics does not require explicit final ordering.
item.evidence_of_dependence: FROM insights WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL AND total_revenue>0
item.alternative: The contract requires “Sort descending by comprehensive_customer_score, then by total_revenue.”
item.reason: The final query omits the required prioritization order.

item.alternative: The contact-current contract says "duplicates from source are preserved," while the overview requires "One row per account_id."
item.reason: Multiple matching contacts would multiply account rows and violate the overview's required grain.

item.statement: Every account with at least one invoice has at least one matching invoice item, so the inner join does not eliminate accounts that require an invoice_item_count of zero.

item.reason: Accounts with invoices but no matching items would receive NULL rather than the required zero.

item.statement: The requested semi-major axis change is the unnormalized difference between successive occupied rounded-hour mean semi-major axes, even when those hours are separated by unequal intervals.

# group duplicate timestamps by mean a; difference consecutive rounded epochs (not necessarily 1h apart)

item.statement: Applying the two-body Kepler relation directly to TLE mean motion produces the semi-major axis intended by the task without additional TLE mean-element corrections.
item.reason: The entire drag series will depend on this conversion from mean motion to semi-major axis.

item.statement: Each consecutive semi-major axis difference should be assigned to the rounded hour of its later TLE epoch.
item.reason: Assigning interval changes to their start or midpoint instead would shift the inferred lag.

item.statement: Rows of t are in chronological epoch order before differencing.
item.reason: Out-of-order rows would produce changes between the wrong chronological neighbors.

item.statement: Positive lag means AP precedes the semi-major axis change, rather than the reverse.
item.reason: The direction determines which time-shifted pairs are searched.

item.statement: OMNI2 columns 0, 1, and 2 represent calendar year, one-based day of year, and zero-based hour of day respectively.
item.reason: These field meanings determine every hourly AP alignment.

item.statement: When multiple TLE epochs round to the same hour, their semi-major axes should be combined by an arithmetic mean before calculating changes.
item.target: hourly_a, hda, rr and printed lag rankings
item.alternative: The task says "TLE epoch times should be rounded to the nearest hour to align with AP measurements," which could mean retaining each TLE-derived change and rounding only its alignment timestamp rather than averaging orbital values first.
item.reason: Averaging before differencing removes within-hour changes and changes the neighboring differences used in every lag comparison.

item.statement: The best lag may be selected by comparing correlations calculated from different sets of drag observations at different lags.
item.reason: The printed sample counts vary across lags, so the ranking can reflect sample composition as well as temporal alignment.
